questions.q: What problem does a port number solve that an IP address alone can't?
options: It identifies which physical cable the traffic should use
It identifies which specific application on a device should receive the traffic
It encrypts the traffic automatically
It determines how fast the connection runs
questions.explain: An IP address gets traffic to the right device; the port number gets it to the right application running on that device.

questions.q: Which port is the standard, well-known port for HTTPS (encrypted web traffic)?
options: Port 80
Port 22
Port 443
Port 3389
questions.explain: Port 443 is the IANA-reserved well-known port for HTTPS. Port 80 is unencrypted HTTP, 22 is SSH, and 3389 is RDP.

options: A fixed port reserved by IANA for a specific service like DNS
A temporary, randomly chosen port the client side of a connection uses, typically in the 49152-65535 range
A port that only works for a single hour before expiring permanently
The port a firewall always blocks by default
questions.explain: Ephemeral ports are temporary, randomly assigned ports used on the initiating (client) side of a connection — different every time a new connection is made.

questions.q: How can a web server handle thousands of simultaneous connections all arriving on port 443 without confusing them?
options: Each connection is uniquely identified by the full combination of source IP, source port, destination IP, and destination port
The server assigns a new IP address to each connecting client
Port 443 automatically splits into sub-ports for each client
Only one connection to port 443 is actually allowed at a time
questions.explain: A connection is uniquely identified by all four values together — the two IP addresses and the two ports — so many clients can all use port 443 on the server side without colliding.

questions.q: Why does a firewall rule name a well-known port like 443 instead of an ephemeral port?
options: Ephemeral ports are always blocked by default, so naming them would be redundant
Well-known ports are the predictable, fixed side of a conversation, while ephemeral ports are different every single time
Firewalls are technically incapable of referencing ephemeral ports
There is no real difference between the two for firewall purposes
questions.explain: A useful firewall rule has to reference something stable — the well-known port is fixed and predictable, while the ephemeral port changes with every new connection.
